description:
FOUND s506f (Opus, 2026-10-04) building -F (perl quotes a plain -F pattern as the STRING q\0PAT\0,
which split compiles as a pattern).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL 618db500):
  pcl  -e 'my @F = split(q{x+}, "axxb"); print "[$F[1]]\n"'   -> []      perl: [b]
  pcl  -e 'my @F = split(q{\.}, "a.b");  print "[$F[1]]\n"'   -> []      perl: [b]
  pcl  -e 'my $p = q{\.}; my @F = split($p, "a.b"); print "[$F[1]]\n"' -> []  perl: [b]
  perl -e 'print scalar(my @x = split("|", "abc")), "\n"'     -> 3 (an empty alternation splits every char)

CAUSE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp p-split's last cond arm ";; Literal string pattern" uses SEARCH on the
string; only a p-regex-match object reaches cl-ppcre.  perl (pp_split) compiles any non-regex EXPR
as a pattern, except the single-space string ' ' (awk mode, already handled).  A pattern string
WITHOUT metacharacters (`split(',', $s)`, the common case) gives the same answer either way, which is
why this survived.

WORKAROUND in s506f: PCLSwitches emits a plain -F pattern as `split(m'PAT')`, so -F is right
regardless.  FIX: route the string through the same scanner path (cache the compiled scanner per
string); probe `split('.', $s)`, `split('|', $s)`, `split('^', $s)` (perl: /^/m), `split(' ', ...)`
stays awk mode, `split(q{ }, ...)` too.  cl/ change: sweep + op/split.t companion.


=== DONE (s507b, Opus 5.5, 2026-10-04) ===
p-split's non-regex operand goes through %p-split-string-pattern: a regex object and " " (awk mode) unchanged; a
string holding a regex metacharacter becomes the memoized match op an interpolated /$p/ builds (%p-regex-parts,
compiled once per string; a bad pattern dies trappably there); a metachar-free string keeps the SEARCH fast path.
Probe table scratch/s507b/p/m2.pl (plain ',', ' ', q{ }, '', '.', '|', '^' (/^/m), '\s+', '\t', "\t", quantifier,
class, `x{2}`, '$', LIMIT, captures with and without LIMIT, every one through a variable, a qr in a variable, a
number 1.5, an invalid '(' in a variable, $_ default, trailing fields) identical to perl; the base differs on 30
rows.  A LITERAL invalid pattern (`split('(', …)`) dies at RUN time where perl dies at compile time -- the same as
PCL's literal `/(/` today.  The -F workaround in tools/lib/PCLSwitches.pm is gone (perl's own text, single-quoted);
Pl/t/pcl-switches-01.t's -F rows pass.  op/split.t 214/5 before and after.  Bench (best of 5, startup subtracted):
splitcomma base 0.462 s / tree 0.423, 0.426 s; splitspace 0.248 / 0.238, 0.252 -- no loss; splitstrre (a regex
STRING) 0.87 s = 6.3x perl, the base answers wrong there.  Guard Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t row 90 (fails on 08de9e4f).
subject: split with a STRING pattern (`split('x+', $s)`, `split($p, $s)`, `split('|', $s)`) splits on the LITERAL text; perl compiles the string as a regex
